item.content:encoded:
This. You could have given such a characterization to practically any major bad guy figure (e.g. Ion, Mr. Rass, the Prophet of Mekhane) and it wouldn't have felt out of place.

As someone who is familiar with Bowe: the supernatural menace Bowe isn't scary. General Bowe is scary because he's a warmongering boot on the throat of humanity who wants to turn the Foundation into an arm of the Pentagon, and succeeds to an extent. The former is a pulp villian; the latter currently exists in the form of several high-level officials in the US government.

item.content:encoded:
Votes don't help the author, so I've vowed to always leave a comment with mine, at the very least whenever I rate an article negatively. If you feel the same, help out by leaving critique with more of your votes. Comment follows:

I don't feel like this tale really did anything. Bearing in mind that both Resurrection and Bowe are new to me, I don't feel like I know who Bowe is and I don't know much about either his situation or his plan. The first half of the tale seems to revel in its genericness, teasing details that are just out of reach. Things start to happen in the second half of the tale, but I couldn't tell you where it's going. You tease plot points that I've not had justified - e.g. "Their terroristic campaign" - but there's no explanation for it.

Overall, I don't really know what's happening here, and I don't really know what purpose this tale serves. -1

item.content:encoded: Well done. Definitely feels like in intro piece, as Bowe hadn't appeared in the Resurrection Canon, other than by name and the affiliation with Omega-7. Excited to see where you're going with it! Resurrection is my favorite Canon by far.

I basically agree with this sentiment, at least as concerns this piece. It works as an introduction/bringing people up to speed bit.

I think that this canon is going to be particularly interesting, as the original team had a very specific idea of where the story was going to go. It doesn't really matter one way or the other, but I am curious if there was any attempt to give the new canons any kind of cohesion with what was planned. Either way, I enjoyed this well enough. +1

This works as a short prelude tale. I'm going into a lot of these contest pieces with the intent that they're being written as segments of a larger narrative, and this one certainly fulfills that role.

It's either that or I just find it amusing that Bowe is being used.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: While the concept of a man rising from his grave to enact vengeance is an appealing thought, I can't say this tale really does it for me. It doesn't do much to characterize General Bowe here (not that he's a character I'm familiar with), but it also doesn't go very far in the direction it's going. I'm left a bit unsatisfied that the tale left off where it did with what little it took the time to set forward.

item.title: Author Post
item.content:encoded:
We'll never get free,
Lamb to the slaughter.
What you gon' do when there's blood in the water?
The price of your greed
Is your son and your daughter
What you gon' do when there's blood in the water?

Howdy hey! I hope you enjoyed the first tale in my teams Canrencon series! I want to thank not_a_seagull, HarryBlank, and The Pighead for all of their wonderful work on this series, without them this would definitely not exist.

As Harry said “I think the whole thing is charmingly surreal. Dude just got tired of being dead, wrote his Christmas list and set his tie straight." Which is honestly pretty accurate.

I would also like to thank my wonderful critters! HarryBlank, not_a_seagull, chiifu, VoidLady, and basicskipreader. They were a wonderful help and they are great!

More are soon to come, but in the meantime you should take a look at my other stuff HERE!
